explanation: The female places her eggs in a pouch on the male's belly, where he fertilizes them. Weeks later his muscles contract and he pushes out the tiny young.

claims.text: Male seahorses carry the eggs in a brood pouch and give birth to the young.
Female seahorses do not carry the eggs to birth, and seahorse parents do not take turns.
The female puts her eggs into the male's pouch, where they are fertilized.
After a few weeks, the male pushes the young out of the pouch with muscular contractions.
